subject: NeuroVista dedicated commit: pool sizing, SKU mapping & remedy ladder
messages:
From: Kyle Peters <kyle@neurovista.io>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Cc: NeuroVista Procurement <procurement@neurovista.io>, Contracts Team <contracts@neurovista.io>
Date: 2027-05-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on Dedicated commit definitions and remedy ladder

Thanks Marcus — attaching the terms our procurement team pulled together (NeuroVista_Requested_Terms_v1.pdf). A few open items we need clarified before we can route redlines: 

1) How do you define a "capacity unit"? Our legal wants a single unambiguous conversion to hardware (e.g., "1 capacity unit = X GPU equivalent / Y vRAM-hours").
2) How do you measure throughput guarantees (is it vram-hours, GPU-hours, or tokens/sec)? We run a mix of short chat and long-batch inference so we care about both sustained throughput and burstability.
3) Service credit ladder — we prefer a cap on credits (insurance won't allow full refunds). Can you provide an explicit ladder with triggers, measurement windows, and cap?
4) Discount schedule — we'd like clarity on how line-item discounts map to committed SKUs vs. actual consumption (especially if we burst beyond reserved).

We're hoping to keep the commercials simple but need the contract language to be precise. Can you send your recommended definitions and an example calculation for our expected profile (roughly 4 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved, with 2x burst allowance)?

Attachments: NeuroVista_Requested_Terms_v1.pdf (requested terms)

Thanks,
Kyle Peters
Head of Platform Partnerships
NeuroVista Inc

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Kyle Peters <kyle@neurovista.io>
Cc: NeuroVista Procurement <procurement@neurovista.io>, Contracts Team <contracts@neurovista.io>
Date: 2027-05-20T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on Dedicated commit definitions and remedy ladder

Kyle — thanks for the precise asks. I've attached a short SKU mapping and a worked example (redwood_capacity_mapping.xlsx) — sending high-level answers below and happy to jump on a 30m call if you prefer.

High-level proposed definitions (working draft):
- Capacity Unit (CU): 1 CU = 1 vram-hour on an A100-80GB equivalent instance. For contract language we can also define as "1 CU = 1 GPU-PU (A100-80GB performance profile)" to avoid ambiguity across hardware families.
- Commitment accounting: Monthly commitment is expressed in CU-hours (e.g., 4 A100 equivalents reserved continuously for a 30-day month = 4 CUs * 24 * 30 = 2880 CU-hours/month).
- Throughput guarantee: Measured as two dimensions — (A) Sustained capacity: CU-hours available per monthly billing period; (B) Latency SLO: p50/p95 inference latency measured against a defined synthetic workload (seq len 256 chat mix) routed to the dedicated pool.
- Burst policy: Customers retain short-term burst allowance (up to 2x committed CU for up to 3 hours/day) as billable overage at the committed discount rate; we can offer an optional burst buffer (pre-purchased pool of CU-hours) to smooth billing.
- Service credits (draft ladder): See spreadsheet, summary below. Credits are applied prorata to monthly commit value and capped at a negotiated percentage.

I'll follow up with internal notes to align on credit ladders and discount table then send a redline-friendly clause set.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Sr. Director, Customer Success — Dedicated & Private
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_capacity_mapping.xlsx

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-20T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Questions on Dedicated commit definitions and remedy ladder — internal proposed redlines

Internal notes / proposed redline items (please comment):

--- Forwarded message ---
From: Kyle Peters <kyle@neurovista.io>
Subject: Questions on Dedicated commit definitions and remedy ladder

1) Capacity Unit (CU): propose we define CU as "1 vram-hour of A100-80GB performance". This avoids vendor-specific model names but ties to perf profile. +1 to include exact micro-bench numbers in appendix.
2) Throughput: measure committed CU as capacity pool; SLA attaches to p50 latency on a defined synthetic profile. If p50 exceeds target for >X% of measured minutes, triggers credit.
3) Ladder: customer prefers a cap. Proposed ladder we should offer: 
   - Monthly uptime >= 99.9% --> 0% credit
   - 99.0% <= uptime < 99.9% --> 5% of monthly commit value
   - 95.0% <= uptime < 99.0% --> 15% credit
   - uptime < 95.0% --> 30% credit cap — propose we cap aggregate credits at 50% of monthly commit (internal concession to customer request).
4) Burst: allow 2x burst for up to 3 hours/day; bill as overage at committed unit price or allow pre-purchased burst pool at 60% of on-demand.

Open items for legal: explicit measurement window (we use rolling 5-minute measurement aggregated to daily), definition of "downtime" vs "degraded performance", and auditability (customers will ask for metric export and root cause write-ups).

Please weigh in on the following before I send to Kyle: 1) cap at 50% vs 100%; 2) 3-hour burst window vs 1-hour; 3) pre-purchase burst pool discounting (60% vs 75%).

--Marcus

Monica — recommend we push for 50% cap and 3-hour burst (improves our flexibility). Aditya — if pricing wants 60% for pre-purchase burst pool we might need to mark special pricing for >12mo commit. Lauren — confirm marketing/packaging language for "CU" and sample math is consistent with docs.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Kyle Peters <kyle@neurovista.io>
Cc: NeuroVista Procurement <procurement@neurovista.io>, Contracts Team <contracts@neurovista.io>
Date: 2027-05-20T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed definitions and example math for NeuroVista commit

Kyle — thanks for the patience. Below is a concise, redline-friendly set of definitions and an example calculation based on your stated profile (4 A100-equivalent appliances reserved; 2x burst allowance). If this matches your intent we can turn it into contract clauses and circulate for signature.

Proposed definitions (final candidate wording):
- "Capacity Unit (CU)": a unit of reserved capacity equal to one vram-hour on a performance profile equivalent to NVIDIA A100-80GB. For clarity: one CU corresponds to the compute capacity required to serve the defined synthetic workload at p50 latency target on an A100-80GB equivalent device for one hour.
- "CU-hour": one Capacity Unit consumed for one hour. Monthly commitments are measured in CU-hours.
- "Committed CU-hours": the CU-hours the customer has prepaid/reserved for the monthly billing period.
- "Burst Allowance": a short duration allowance permitting the customer to exceed the Committed CU-hours rate by up to 2x for up to 3 hours per calendar day; overage beyond the Burst Allowance will be billed as described in the pricing schedule.
- "Throughput & Latency SLO": Redwood will measure p50 and p95 latency for a defined synthetic workload (seq len 256 chat mix). The p50 latency SLO applies to 95% of the measured samples in the monthly aggregation window.

Service credit ladder (measurement & remedy):
- Measurement window: rolling 5-minute intervals aggregated across the monthly period; incidents are reported with timestamped metrics and RCA within 5 business days.
- Ladder (applies to monthly invoice amount for the committed CU-hours portion):
   * Monthly availability >= 99.9%: 0% credit
   * 99.0% <= availability < 99.9%: 5% credit
   * 95.0% <= availability < 99.0%: 15% credit
   * availability < 95.0%: 30% credit
- Credit cap: aggregate credits for a single monthly billing period are capped at 50% of the monthly committed CU-hours value (negotiable).

Example commit math (worked example):
- Customer target: reserve 4 A100-equivalent devices continuously.
- Monthly CU-hour calculation: 4 CUs * 24 hours * 30 days = 2880 CU-hours/month.
- If NeuroVista uses additional burst beyond the Burst Allowance, overage billed at committed unit price (no surcharge) unless pre-purchased burst pool is used.
- If availability for the month measured at 98.4%: credit = 15% of monthly committed CU-hours value (per ladder). If the credit calculation would exceed 50% cap we apply the cap.

Attachments: redwood_capacity_mapping.xlsx contains mapping of common GPU classes to CU equivalents and sample pricing rows for 12/24/36 month commits.

Next steps: 1) confirm the 50% credit cap is acceptable; 2) confirm burst window (we suggested 3 hours/day); 3) we can produce contract-ready language for section: "Definitions — Capacity & Remedies" and attach as an amendment to your draft.

If convenient, I can book a 30m call today to walk through the example with procurement and contracts.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Sr. Director, Customer Success — Dedicated & Private
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_capacity_mapping.xlsx

Marcus — this is very helpful, thanks. Quick notes from our side: 

1) The CU definition looks fine; we'll ask legal to include the appendix with micro-bench numbers but no objection to tying to A100-80GB performance profile.
2) For the ladder, procurement still wants the credit cap lower — their preference is 50% maximum (we can agree to that). Please confirm the cap is applied only to the committed portion (not any overage billing).
3) Burst window: 3 hours/day is acceptable. We will need a short clause that allows one-off exceptions (e.g., planned scale events) with 7 days notice.
4) Deliverables: please send the contract-ready clause set and the DocuSign offer. Also include the SOC2 artifact link for our security team to ingest (we asked earlier in the questionnaire).
